bug_semantics: Bandit's HTTP/2 connection handler appends each received chunk to state.buffer and repeatedly calls Frame.deserialize/2. The oversized-frame clause introduced to enforce max_frame_size destructured not only the 9-byte HTTP/2 header but also _payload::binary-size(length), so an attacker could announce a 24-bit length up to 16,777,215 bytes and keep the parser returning {:more, msg} until that entire body had accumulated. The length > max_frame_size guard therefore ran only after the excessive allocation, allowing unauthenticated h2/h2c peers to amplify per-connection buffering far beyond the negotiated 16 KiB default and cause memory-exhaustion denial of service.
flaw_origin: Commit f00dd69a5b2a4863be585907acd853c4ffd41399 added max_frame_size enforcement to lib/bandit/http2/frame.ex and passed state.connection.local_settings.max_frame_size from lib/bandit/http2/handler.ex, but wrote the rejecting clause with _payload::binary-size(length) before the length > max_frame_size guard. This made the newly introduced size check causally too late; the same commit's generic fallback continued to request more bytes for a header whose declared body was not yet complete.
ai_marker: absent: the exact BIC commit object names author Mat Trudel <mat@geeky.net> and committer Mat Trudel <mat@geeky.net>; its message has no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, or other AI trailer, and neither identity is a bot
evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/mtrudel/bandit/security/advisories/GHSA-q6v9-r226-v65f identifies lib/bandit/http2/frame.ex:23-65, explains that every oversized-frame check required payload::binary-size(length), demonstrates continued buffering after a 0xFFFFFF-length header, and names 1.11.0 as patched. Its rendered affected boundary is > 0.3.5 and < 1.11.0; the assigned bundle's normalized range says >= 0.3.5, but repository tags resolve the boundary unambiguously as described below.

History search `git log main --full-history --reverse -p -L 22,75:lib/bandit/http2/frame.ex` and exact-string search `git log --all --reverse -S'_payload::binary-size(length)' -- lib/bandit/http2/frame.ex` identify f00dd69a5b2a4863be585907acd853c4ffd41399 as the first and smallest commit to write the flawed oversized-frame clause; the only later removal is the fix 1e8e55966da9129016b73d32f0e1df4630e3b463. The BIC is an ordinary one-parent commit, not a move, revert, merge, release commit, or squash aggregate.

At f00dd69a5b2a4863be585907acd853c4ffd41399, `git blame -L 33,46 -- lib/bandit/http2/frame.ex` attributes the entire new oversized-frame clause to that commit, including line 40 `_payload::binary-size(length)` and line 43 `when length > max_frame_size`. `git blame -L 28,29 -- lib/bandit/http2/handler.ex` attributes line 28, which supplies `state.connection.local_settings.max_frame_size`, to the same BIC.

Direct-parent verification: `git show c7bfd639f8f07971090a6b8c009a8067589b9f44:lib/bandit/http2/frame.ex` shows only deserialize/1, no max_frame_size argument, no length > max_frame_size guard, and no oversized-frame rejection clause. `git diff c7bfd639f8f07971090a6b8c009a8067589b9f44 f00dd69a5b2a4863be585907acd853c4ffd41399 -- lib/bandit/http2/frame.ex lib/bandit/http2/handler.ex` proves that the BIC added those exact vulnerable lines and wired the negotiated limit into the buffering path.

Affected-boundary verification: tags 0.3.5=f1976e96be5afedb0ae7920301b7b8047b4703d1 and 0.3.6=3d4da2f7b0415f426bbb972ef0465a479043c6c2. `git tag --contains f00dd69a5b2a4863be585907acd853c4ffd41399` starts at 0.3.6, not 0.3.5, and `git diff 0.3.5 0.3.6 -- lib/bandit/http2/frame.ex lib/bandit/http2/handler.ex` shows the late oversized-frame check appearing across that release boundary. Thus repository history corroborates the first-party page's strict `> 0.3.5` lower bound and exposes the bundle's `>= 0.3.5` normalization discrepancy without leaving the causal boundary unresolved.

Fix evidence: first-party commit URL https://github.com/mtrudel/bandit/commit/1e8e55966da9129016b73d32f0e1df4630e3b463 points to the one-parent direct source fix. Its diff moves the length > max_frame_size clause ahead of body-bearing clauses and changes its pattern to consume only the 9-byte header plus currently available rest, so rejection no longer waits for the declared payload. It also adds test/bandit/http2/frame_deserialization_test.exs coverage using a 16,385-byte declaration with only the 9-byte header.

Patched-boundary verification: tags 1.10.4=dea432ec1ec94eee4b9ad0219b09a568c4ccb960 and 1.11.0=e62619895d0d2584d7ffa57d43ef6f72437dfaff. `git tag --contains 1e8e55966da9129016b73d32f0e1df4630e3b463 --list '1.10.4' '1.11.0'` returns only 1.11.0, while `git diff 1.10.4 1.11.0 -- lib/bandit/http2/frame.ex test/bandit/http2/frame_deserialization_test.exs` shows exactly the header-only rejection and regression coverage. `git blame 1e8e55966da9129016b73d32f0e1df4630e3b463 -L 28,40 -- lib/bandit/http2/frame.ex` attributes the fixed header-only clause directly to that SHA.

BIC-only AI inspection: `git cat-file -p f00dd69a5b2a4863be585907acd853c4ffd41399` shows author and committer Mat Trudel <mat@geeky.net> and the message `Raise error when receiving oversized frame` with explanatory prose but no AI/co-author/generated trailer. No other commit object was used to attribute AI authorship to the introduction.
reasoning: The first-party advisory defines a late size-check vulnerability, not merely the older parser's general need to receive a complete valid frame. Source history shows that f00dd69a5b2a4863be585907acd853c4ffd41399 is where Bandit first attempted to enforce the negotiated max_frame_size and simultaneously encoded the mistake: the rejecting pattern required the full declared payload before evaluating the oversize guard, while the handler retained partial data and requested more. Its direct parent lacks the max-size API and the flawed rejection clause, and the first release containing it is 0.3.6, consistent with the advisory page's strict lower bound. The direct fix 1e8e55966da9129016b73d32f0e1df4630e3b463 makes the rejection header-only and is first shipped in 1.11.0. Because the proven smallest BIC's own commit object is human-authored and human-committed with no AI marker or trailer, the required BIC-only attribution decision is NOT_AI.
